# Psalm 88 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A song. A psalm of the descendants of Korah. For the choir director: according to Mahalath Leannoth. A contemplative poem of Heman the Ezrahite.

**2** LORD, God who saves me — I've been crying out to you day and night.

**3** Please let my prayer reach you! Turn your ear toward my cries.

**4** My soul is drowning in trouble, and my life is sliding toward the grave.

**5** I'm already counted among those going to their death; I'm like someone who has no strength left.

**6** I've been tossed in with the dead — like corpses lying in the grave, people you've forgotten, cut off from your care.

**7** You've thrown me into the deepest, darkest pit.

**8** Your fury crushes me; wave after wave of your anger crashes over me. Selah

**9** You've driven all my friends away from me; you've made me repulsive to them. I'm trapped with no way out.

**10** My eyes are worn out from crying. Every single day I call out to you, LORD, reaching my hands toward you.

**11** Do you perform miracles for the dead? Do ghosts stand up and praise you? Selah

**12** Does anyone in the grave talk about your faithful love? Does anyone in the place of destruction mention your reliability?

**13** Does anyone in the pitch dark know about your wonders? Does anyone in the land of oblivion experience your justice?

**14** But I keep crying out to you, LORD! Every morning my prayer is waiting for you.

**15** LORD, why do you push me away? Why do you turn your face from me?

**16** I've been suffering and near death since I was young. I've endured your terrors until I'm paralyzed.

**17** Your fury has rolled right over me; your onslaughts have wiped me out.

**18** They surround me like floodwaters all day long; they close in from every side.

**19** You've taken away everyone I love — every friend, every companion. Darkness is my only friend now.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **88:1-18**: This is the Bible's darkest prayer — bar none. It begins in darkness and ends in darkness. There is no resolution, no silver lining, no 'but God.' And yet it's included in Scripture, which means God accepts prayers that don't have happy endings.

- **88:19**: 'Darkness is my only friend.' That's the last word. The fact that this psalm exists in the Bible is itself a profound theological statement: you can bring your worst despair to God, even if nothing changes.

— PNEUMA
